instruction.text: Jane uses a measuring container to measure amounts of water. How many litres of water are in the container?

atoms.b: There is <mat><gap>1</gap></mat> litre of water in the measuring container.
There are <mat><gap>2</gap></mat> litres of water in the measuring container.
There are <mat><gap>5</gap></mat> litres of water in the measuring container.
There are <mat><gap>7</gap></mat> litres of water in the measuring container.

instruction.text: Jane swaps her measuring container to a smaller one that uses millilitres. How many millilitres of water are in the container?

hint.text: Another unit for measuring capacity is millilitres. One litre is the same as 1,000 millilitres. The unit symbol for millilitres is ml.

atoms.b: There are <mat><gap>125</gap></mat> ml of water in the container.
atoms.sound: There are 125 millilitres of water in the container.

atoms.b: There are <mat><gap>250</gap></mat> ml of water in the container.
atoms.sound: There are 250 millilitres of water in the container.

atoms.b: There are <mat><gap>700</gap></mat> ml of water in the container.
atoms.sound: There are 700 millilitres of water in the container.

atoms.b: There are <mat><gap>1000</gap></mat> ml of water in the container.
atoms.sound: There are 1000 millilitres of water in the container.

atoms.b: There are <mat><gap>1250</gap></mat> ml of water in the container.
